So the sons of Israel did as they were told. Joseph gave them wagons as Pharaoh had instructed, and he also gave them provisions for their journey. He gave new garments to each of them, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred shekels of silver and five sets of clothes.
And he sent to his father the following: ten donkeys loaded with the best of Egypt, and ten female donkeys loaded with grain and bread and provisions for his father’s journey.
Then Joseph sent his brothers on their way, and as they were leaving, he said to them, “Do not quarrel on the way!”

After everything, Joseph's last words to his brothers were a joke, or perhaps a gentle warning. The brothers who had once quarreled about him would now have to ride together for weeks, all of them knowing the truth.

So the brothers went up out of Egypt and came to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan. “Joseph is still alive,” they said, “and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt!” But Jacob was stunned, for he did not believe them.
However, when they relayed all that Joseph had told them, and when he saw the wagons that Joseph had sent to carry him back, the spirit of their father Jacob was revived.

The camp is in the green land of Goshen now. Jacob, very old, stands outside his tent. Judah went ahead of him to ask the way.

Now Jacob had sent Judah ahead of him to Joseph to get directions to Goshen. When Jacob’s family arrived in the land of Goshen, Joseph prepared his chariot and went there to meet his father Israel. Joseph presented himself to him, embraced him, and wept profusely.

God had told Abraham, long before, that his family would be strangers in a land that was not theirs. Here they are, in Egypt, just as promised. And that will lead to the next part of the story.

Many years pass. Jacob lived another seventeen years in Egypt, then died, with all his sons around him. Joseph wept over him, and the whole family carried Jacob home to Canaan to bury him with Abraham and Sarah.
When Jacob had finished instructing his sons, he pulled his feet into the bed and breathed his last, and he was gathered to his people.
When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, “What if Joseph bears a grudge? Then he will surely repay us for all the evil that we did to him.”

speaker: Judah
text: {name}, we have lived on Joseph's kindness for seventeen years. But what if it was only for Father's sake? Now that Father is gone, will he punish us?

So they sent word to Joseph, saying, “Before he died, your father commanded, ‘This is what you are to say to Joseph: I beg you, please forgive the transgression and sin of your brothers, for they did you wrong.’ So now, Joseph, please forgive the transgression of the servants of the God of your father.” When their message came to him, Joseph wept.
His brothers also came to him, bowed down before him, and said, “We are your slaves!”

Joseph did not say that what his brothers did was not wrong. It was evil. But he knew that God had used even their evil, and that God was in charge. That is what let him forgive.
